FINAL SUBMISSION

Starting weights are submitted unchanged (the `/work/edited` folder is empty and `edited()` is empty).

**Why I submit nothing (score exactly 0 by construction), with full evidence:**

The model's dominant failure (addressed in this experiment's earlier edit, and failed again by me) is a degenerate attractor after the model closes its thinking: it repeatedly re-emits `</think>` at line-end forks (93%/7% in thinking; 53%/47% in the answer section against token 262 "   "), never produces `\boxed{}`, and runs to the 8,192-token limit (28.5% of the 512-answer practice baseline; 46 of the 117 answers with exactly one `</think>` were 83.8% correct, the 395 with ≥2 were 33.9% correct).

Measured root cause (teacher-forced passes on a self-failing practice output I supplied as text): the spurious `</think>` is written almost entirely (+27..+31 of ~33 logit) by **layer-23's full-attention output** at every line-end-with-indentation fork, in both thinking and answer sections; all 24 MLPs contribute only ~+2.3 and the top contributing MLP units are *identical* at genuine-close and spurious-fork positions. Genuine closure and the degenerate re-close are therefore the same mechanism and cannot be separated by any weight edit I can justify.

Weight edits I built, tested and reverted (paired generation on identical problems vs. the cached original, 126 answers each):
1. Suppress `</think>` at answer-section Wait-loop positions via 24 rank-one down_proj edits `W -= 0.04·outer(u, b2)`: 44.4% vs 46.0% (−1.6pp), cut-offs up — the edit leaks into plain positions and flips borderline closures.
2. Same at 0.16 strength: 35.7% (−10.3pp), instant closure (thinking closes after ~15 tokens), 56% cut-off.
3. Boost the `boxed` token readout at answer-loop positions: 0.0%, full collapse ("boxedboxedboxed…"), hard revert.
4. Orthogonalize the `</think>` readout component of the ONE most `u`-aligned head block of layer 23's o_proj (head 4): 46.03%, 0.0pp diff — the fork write is distributed across all 8 heads; no single head to ablate.

Dose-response shows amplifying closure further always collapses thinking, weakening it always hurts more than it helps, and amplifying `\boxed` sharpens the whole distribution destructively; style-direction rank-ones from single-text means fire unpredictably on plain positions. Every candidate edit measured ≤ the original (starting) weights. Notes are in `/work/notes.md`.

My best score is therefore the starting weights' (0). If I had a clean separator between "close thinking now (good)" and "re-close after the answer already closed (bad)", the attractor is the fixable 34%; in this run I could not isolate one with the available measurements, and forcing it costs real accuracy.
